title: Cabell-Huntington Health Department joins statewide health initiative - NewsBreak
text: HUNTINGTON, WV (WOWK) – Whether it’s going for a hike or just walking up the stairs, chances are you’re active in your daily life without even thinking much about it. That’s why the Cabell-Huntington Health Department is taking part in Active Southern West Virginia’s new “Move More Challenge,” which encourages folks to be active in every day parts of their lives. “The Move More Challenge is anyone throughout the state. But for our health department, we are promoting it among our staff. And then, we also want to just raise awareness to other businesses and organizations that they too can create a culture of health by just starting small,” Prevention Coordinator for the Cabell-Huntington Health Department Casey Napier said. The Move More Challenge is a spin off of Gov. Patrick Morrissey’s Mountaineer Mile, with an added twist. It encourages West Virginians to find activity in their everyday lives and build upon it. “We’re trying to encourage people to take whatever steps they can to improve their activity level. If you walk a little bit, walk a little bit more. If you don’t like to walk, let’s look at another activity that you do that actually has exercise benefit. And, let’s get you doing that a little bit more. And, those are the kind of things that help people get healthy,” Dr. Michael Kilkenny, MD, MS, CEO and Health Officer for the Cabell-Huntington Health Department, said. The initiative launched on June 9, and it lasts for six weeks. You can sign up here and track your progress. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WOWK 13 News.
